name: Jeju Island: Jeju City, Seogwipo, Seongsan and Aewol

cities.base: The old town around Tapdong and Dongmun market: Gwandeokjeong, the market, Samseonghyeol and Yongduam are all within 3 km, and the airport bus is about 1,000 won.
cities.name: Jeju City

cities.base: Seogwi-dong, by Lee Jung Seop Street and the Maeil Olle market: the port, two waterfalls and dinner on foot; Andeok and Jungmun need a car or bus.
cities.name: Seogwipo

cities.base: Seongsan-eup, below Ilchulbong, so the dawn climb is a walk and the Udo ferry and the Haenyeo Museum are short rides.
cities.name: Seongsan

cities.base: The Aewol coast road, near the cafes and Noraba; Hallim Park and Hyeopjae are 12 to 15 km south-west, so you want a car.
cities.name: Aewol

places.name: Donsadon (Main Branch)
places.note: Coal-grilled Jeju black pork; the 600 g set is 66,000 won for two. No dinner reservations, so arrive before 17:30, last order 21:15, closed Tuesdays. Hours vary, check.

places.name: Ollae Guksu (Main Branch)
places.note: One dish, gogi-guksu, pork noodle soup at 8,500 won (a visitor paid 10,000). The line moves fast; no dinner, closed Sundays and at Seollal and Chuseok. Hours vary, check.

places.name: Ujin Haejangguk
places.note: Order the gosari yukgaejang, bracken soup at 9,000 won, the island's hangover cure. You take a numbered ticket and peak waits run 1 to 2 hours, so go at 07:00. Closed Lunar New Year and Chuseok.

places.name: Sangchunjae
places.note: Bibimbap with ssamjang from 12,000 won, and grilled mackerel; expect a wait. Lunch only, closed Mondays (and the first-week Tuesday per one listing). Hours vary, check.

places.name: Dombedon
places.note: Black pork ogyeopsal, the five-layer belly, at around 20,000 won a head, and an English-speaking manager. Open daily until 22:30.

places.name: Jeju Folklore and Natural History Museum
places.note: Four halls on Jeju's natural history and folk life, next to Samseonghyeol. One listing gives about 1.50 dollars and a visitor says free, so check the price. Closed Mondays.

places.name: Jeju National Museum
places.note: The permanent exhibition is free and covers the island's past; budget 90 minutes. Closed Mondays. Also the bad-weather fallback when Hallasan is off.

places.name: Arario Museum Tapdong Cinema
places.note: A converted cinema showing contemporary art, with Warhol and Subodh Gupta on show. A visitor calls the ticket somewhat expensive: check the price. Hours vary, check.

places.name: Samseonghyeol
places.note: Three holes in the ground where Jeju's founding legend says the island's first three men rose; the shrine dates from 1526. Admission is not listed, so check the price. 45 minutes.

places.name: Gwandeokjeong Pavilion
places.note: A 15th-century pavilion, among the island's oldest buildings, in the old government office complex; about 1,500 won. Open until 21:30 Wednesday to Sunday, 18:00 Monday and Tuesday.

places.name: Yongduam Rock
places.note: A lava rock on the shore 2 km from the old town, with 17,000 Google reviews to prove the crowds. Free and open around the clock; 30 minutes, best on the way to dinner.

places.name: Jeju 4.3 Peace Park
places.note: The memorial to the 14,000 to 30,000 people killed in the 1948 to 1951 uprising; give it two hours, and come before the National Museum, not after. Admission is not listed: check the price.

places.name: Halla Arboretum
places.note: Free gardens and woodland paths in the south of the city, 90 minutes on foot. The quiet answer to a day when the Hallasan trails are shut.

places.name: Jeju Stone Park
places.note: A park of the island's volcanic stone, 18 km east of town, two hours. Listings disagree on the fee, so check the price. Closed Mondays.

places.name: Dongmun Traditional Market
places.note: The city's big daily market, free to wander, 35,000 Google reviews. Open from 08:00 to 21:00 every day; go hungry in the evening.

places.name: Oneunjeong Gimbap
places.note: Takeaway only: gimbap with tempura flakes, 3,000 won plain or 4,500 with tuna or tteokgalbi. Call ahead, it shuts for a break around 13:00 to 14:30, closed Sundays. Hours vary, check.

places.name: Chunshim
places.note: Galchi, hairtail, grilled whole for 78,000 won for two, deboned at the table; braised is 65,000. Break 15:30 to 17:00, closed Thursdays per one listing. Hours vary, check.

places.name: Twins Raw Fish Restaurant
places.note: Raw fish by Seogwipo port: the lunch sashimi bibimbap is 10,000 won, the special for two 70,000 to 100,000 in the evening. Open daily.

places.name: Seogwipo Maeil Olle Market
places.note: A covered market running since the 1960s, free to walk. Open daily 07:00 to 21:00; the evening is the time.

places.name: Lee Jung Seop Street
places.note: The street where the painter lived and worked, free to walk. The art museum's main building is closed until 2027; a free archive show sits on the 2nd floor of the Creative Studio.

places.name: Lee Jung-seop Refuge
places.note: The house where Lee Jung-seop lived for about a year as a Korean War refugee; neighbours still live next door, so keep quiet. Fee not listed, check the price; hours vary, check.

places.name: Jusangjeolli Cliff
places.note: Hexagonal basalt columns along about 2 km of coast; around 2,000 won, 45 minutes. Combine with Yakcheonsa, 2 km east.

places.name: Yakcheonsa Temple
places.note: A temple in Daepo, 2 km east of Jusangjeolli, free and open around the clock, so pair the two; 45 minutes, rated 4.4 by about 2,400 visitors.

places.name: Bonte Museum
places.note: Opened 2012, galleries tied together by Tadao Ando gardens; about 20 to 23 dollars, give it two hours. Open daily 10:00 to 18:00.

places.name: Osulloc Tea Museum
places.note: The busiest museum on the island, 24,000 Google reviews; visitors say admission is free, but check the price. Go at 09:00 before the coaches. 75 minutes.

places.name: Cheonjiyeon Falls
places.note: A three-tier fall about 22 m high in subtropical forest, with giant mottled eels in the pond; 2,500 won. One source says open to 22:00, another to 17:50, so hours vary, check.

places.name: Jeongbang Falls
places.note: A 23 m fall that drops straight into the sea, the only one in Korea; 2,000 won, free over 65, five minutes down a pine stairway. Also a site of the 4.3 events. Hours vary, check.

places.name: Oedolgae Sea Stack
places.note: A 20 m rock stack on Olle Route 7, free; legend says General Choe Yeong dressed it as a giant soldier. Come at sunset for Beomseom island behind it.

places.name: Ojo Haenyeo's House
places.note: Run by the Ojo women divers: order the abalone porridge with the innards, from 11,000 won. Opens at 07:00, so it is breakfast after Ilchulbong at dawn. Hours vary, check.

places.name: Gommak Sikdang
places.note: Hoe-guksu, cold noodles with raw fish, at 11,000 won, or sea urchin noodles at 12,000. Last order 20:00; closed the 1st and 3rd Tuesday, so do not plan it on a Tuesday.

places.name: Myeongjin Jeonbok
places.note: Abalone from the haenyeo: porridge 12,000 won, stone-pot rice 15,000, but those are 2023 prices, so expect more. A 30 minute wait is normal; closed Tuesdays, last order 20:00.

places.name: Seongsan Ilchulbong
places.note: A 182 m tuff cone, UNESCO since 2007. Opens an hour before sunrise, so climb for dawn; closes 20:00 Nov to Feb, 21:00 Mar to Oct. Fee not found, check the price.

places.name: Jeju Haenyeo Museum
places.note: The story of the island's women divers, who numbered over 23,000 in 1965. Under a dollar; 90 minutes; closed Mondays.

places.name: Udo Island
places.note: A small island off Seongsan, half a day by ferry; a visitor paid about 8,000 won for the island bus tour. Ferry times and fares not confirmed, check the price.

places.name: Yumin Art Nouveau Collection
places.note: Art nouveau glass in a Tadao Ando building, with Ilchulbong framed across the water. Price not found, check the price; hours vary, check.

places.name: Geomun Oreum
places.note: A UNESCO volcanic cone with nine peaks and a 4 hour route, capped at 300 hikers a day, so ask about booking ahead. Last start 14:00, closed Tuesdays; fee not found, check the price.

places.name: Manjanggul Lava Tube
places.note: A UNESCO lava tube 8.9 km long, of which 1 km is open, entered by No. 2. Hours and fee not found: hours vary, check, and check the price.

places.name: Jeju Folk Village
places.note: A reconstructed 1890s village of more than 100 buildings; 15,000 won, two and a half hours. Open daily.

places.name: Seongeup Folk Village
places.note: A walled county town about 600 years old, the county office here from 1423. Hours and fee not found, check the price; hours vary, check.

places.name: Noraba
places.note: Seafood ramen with prawns, squid and abalone, the octopus one at 15,000 won, over the sea. Break 14:00 to 15:00 and it shuts around 16:30, so make it lunch. Hours vary, check.

places.name: Yi Chun-ok Mackerel Ssambap
places.note: Braised mackerel with aged kimchi, grilled hairtail, abalone porridge; 15,000 to 40,000 won a head. Break 16:00 to 17:00, closed Tuesdays per its own site. Hours vary, check.

places.name: Donhaesang
places.note: Jeju black pork, five-layer belly or neck at 22,000 won a portion, kimchi stew 9,000, near Hyeopjae. Open 10:00 to 21:00; closed days not stated.

places.name: Biyangnol
places.note: A cafe for scones and coffee looking out at Biyangdo island; price not checked. Open daily 11:00 to 20:00, best for the late-afternoon light.

places.name: Jeju Beer Brewery
places.note: A 40 minute self-guided audio tour, about 13 dollars, mostly in Korean, ending with tap beer you only get on the island. Last entry before 18:00.

places.name: Hallim Park
places.note: Opened 1971: palm road, bonsai and water gardens, and the Hyeopjae and Ssangyong lava caves; 15,000 won. Ticket sales end 16:30 in winter, later from March. Two hours.

places.name: Hangpaduri Anti-Mongol Historic Site
places.note: The earthen fort the Sambyeolcho built in 1271 against the Mongols; it fell in April 1273 to a Goryeo-Yuan army of 12,000. Free; open from 08:30 in summer, to 17:30 in winter.

places.name: Saebyeol Oreum
places.note: A 519 m volcanic cone, 20 to 30 minutes up (the west side is steeper), with the west coast and Biyangdo below. Silver grass in autumn; fee not stated.

places.name: Kim Tschang-Yeul Museum of Art
places.note: The water-drop painter's museum, about 1.50 dollars; visitors say it holds few works, so an hour is plenty. Closed Mondays.

places.name: Greek Mythology Museum
places.note: A rainy-day hour of Greek-myth art in Hallim; the only price seen is 9,000 won from 2018, so check the price. Open 09:00 to 18:00.

outings.why: Baengnokdam, 9.6 km each way, 5 to 6 hours up and 4 to 5 down; book on visithalla.jeju.go.kr (1,000 a day, opens the 1st of the month at 09:00 for the next). Start by 07:00 to pass Azalea Field Shelter by about noon.
outings.name: Hallasan summit by the Seongpanak trail
outings.fallback: Halla Arboretum, free, 09:00 to 18:00, or the free Jeju National Museum.

outings.why: The steeper summit route, 8.7 km each way, 4.5 to 5.5 hours up; reservation required, 500 a day, and a no-show earns a 3-month ban. Checkpoint at Samgakbong Shelter.
outings.name: Hallasan summit by the Gwaneumsa trail
outings.fallback: Halla Arboretum, free, 09:00 to 18:00, or the free Jeju National Museum.

outings.why: No reservation: Eorimok climbs to the Manse Dongsan ridge at 1,700 m and Yeongsil runs 5.8 km to Witseoreum, 3 to 4 hours together. Bus 240 from Jeju City takes 40 minutes, 1,200 won.
outings.name: Hallasan by the Eorimok and Yeongsil trails

destination.name: Jeju Island: Jeju City, Seogwipo, Seongsan and Aewol
destination.pitch: Six days on a volcanic island with a car: three nights in Jeju City for the museums and black pork, then Seogwipo's waterfalls, Ilchulbong at dawn from Seongsan, and the quieter west coast at Aewol.
destination.caveat: Jeju is a car island: the bus to Seongsan takes 90 minutes and the west loop through Aewol two hours, and many places sit 15 to 25 km from town. Hallasan summit trails need a permit, released on the 1st of the month before, and listed hours often disagree. Put together for you just now from a live search, so check anything you're pinning the trip on.

because.food: Black pork grilled over coal at Donsadon and Dombedon, gogi-guksu at Ollae Guksu, abalone porridge from the women divers at Ojo, and hairtail deboned at the table at Chunshim.
because.nature: Hallasan in the middle, Seongsan Ilchulbong's tuff cone, Manjanggul's 8.9 km lava tube, Jusangjeolli's basalt columns and Jeongbang, a waterfall that drops into the sea.
because.culture: The 4.3 Peace Park on the 1948 to 1951 killings, the Haenyeo Museum, Gwandeokjeong from the 15th century, Seongeup's 600-year-old walled town and the 1271 Hangpaduri fort.
because.adventure: Hallasan's summit is a 9 to 11 hour day on a booked permit, Geomun Oreum caps hikers at 300 a day, and Ilchulbong opens an hour before sunrise.
because.relaxation: Seogwipo's evening market, scones over the sea at Biyangnol and Hallim Park's gardens make easy days between the climbs.
because.exploration: Four corners of one island, each an hour or two apart: the old town, the south-coast falls, the east with Udo, the west with Hallim and the oreums.
